headline_findings: 0623 s4 'all of the paper did their experiment at outdoor' is FALSE - Lin et al. (5G Spectrum Learning, ICCC 2023) ran an explicit INDOOR scene with a DJI Phantom 4 hovering 5-10 m from a USRP-B210.

0721 s13 CISSIR row is FALSE on every cell - CISSIR has a single target at 40 m with 'Target radar cross section 1 m2' (Table I.D), i.e. family 'Injected', not 'None'; and CISSIR is not an NVIDIA paper.
0721 s13 takeaway 'the only small drone' is contradicted by the deck's own table (LAMBDA and Great-X are both low-alt UAV). The 'only SBR+PO' half survives.

0630 LaSen: 'on the live 5G downlink' is FALSE - LaSen's drone echoes come from its own USRP transmitter (MATLAB PDSCH+DM-RS waveform); real gNB captures are used only to build RE-occupancy masks. Affects 4 claims.
0630 s10 'Reuses reference signals (CSI-RS / SSB)' is FALSE - LaSen's estimator uses PDSCH + DM-RS; SSB appears only as a power threshold for occupancy masking.

0630 s15 'earlier 5G sensing: only the sparse pilots' is FALSE for OUR surveyed passive corpus (Renyi 2022 / IRS 2023 / Asilomar 2025 all use full reference-channel CAF). It is true only of LaSen's own monostatic comparison set.

Ground-truth slide (0623 s7 / 0630 s2): there are THREE tracking papers in the deck's own tables, not two (Milani et al. 2021 tracks with an IMM filter and shows GPS ground truth); and LIPASE's DGPS is SUB-METER, not centimetre.

0721 s12 'Sionna returns only a path gain' is FALSE - Sionna RT returns complex scattered-field components (Technical Report Eq. 168). The defensible claim is only 'no coherent PO/Kirchhoff surface integral, and no RCS output'.
0721 s11 Omega = 4pi/N is VERBATIM correct - Sionna RT Technical Report Sec. 3.1.1 p.16: 'ray tubes sharing approximately the same opening angle 4pi/N_S'.

wrong_items.paper: LaSen: Low-Altitude Drone Sensing with 5G-NR Signals (ACM/IEEE SenSys, 2026)
wrong_items.claim: 'Tracks low-altitude drones (range + velocity) on the live 5G downlink'
wrong_items.why: FALSIFIED. LaSen's drone echoes are NOT captured off a live commercial downlink - they come from LaSen's own USRP transmitter: 'During flying, LaSen continually transmits NR signals with full resource allocation while simultaneously activating the receiver for capturing. For simplicity, hereafter we refer to this configuration as the "full-band" mode' (Sec. 6.1.1); the waveform is MATLAB-generated PDSCH+DM-RS (Sec. 5). Real gNBs enter only as occupancy statistics: 'We capture and demodulate 2200 data frames from two China Mobile N41 band gNBs in our campus ... resulting in a binary mask indicating the RE occupation pattern. The final channel frequency response was obtained by performing element-wise multiplication between the full-band drone measurements and the derived occupancy masks'.

wrong_items.paper: LaSen: Low-Altitude Drone Sensing with 5G-NR Signals (ACM/IEEE SenSys, 2026)
wrong_items.claim: 'Reuses reference signals (CSI-RS / SSB) and data signals (PDSCH)'

CSI-RS and SSB appear only as the MOTIVATION (their low 200 Hz / 50 Hz rates) and SSB additionally only as a masking threshold: 'We use the maximum power within an SSB group as a threshold T_ssb' (Sec. 6.1.1). wrong_items.claim: 'The limit — earlier 5G sensing: Only the sparse pilots → too few samples (sub-Nyquist) → the track keeps breaking up' (earlier 5G sensing did NOT use the data channel)
wrong_items.why: FALSIFIED for the surveyed corpus. The 5G passive-radar papers in our own survey do NOT use only pilots - they cross-correlate a full reference channel against the surveillance channel over the whole downlink (Abratkiewicz 2022: 22 CAF references + reference/surveillance channel model; Maksymiuk IRS 2023: 12 CAF references, 'xref - baseband digitized reference signal'; Maksymiuk Asilomar 2025: 'the radar receives the direct wave through a reference channel'). Their stated limit is idle / low-occupancy time, not pilot-only sampling. The 'pilots only' framing is true of LaSen's own monostatic comparison set (CSI-RS/DM-RS/PRS works), not of our passive corpus.

wrong_items.paper: LaSen: Low-Altitude Drone Sensing with 5G-NR Signals (ACM/IEEE SenSys, 2026)
wrong_items.claim: Notes: 'It then solves the whole thing as a sparse-recovery problem, and gets continuous tracking on a live 5G downlink with no extra spectrum'
wrong_items.why: The sparse-recovery half is EXACT ('LaSen formulates the tracking of UAVs as a sparse recovery problem'). 'on a live 5G downlink' is falsified - see idx 79.

wrong_items.claim: 'Sionna returns only a path gain for the drone — it never integrates the scattering over the target surface'
wrong_items.why: HALF FALSIFIED. Sionna RT does NOT return 'only a path gain': it returns complex field/channel coefficients. Technical Report Eq. (168) gives the diffusely scattered field explicitly - 'the diffusely scattered field Es(r) at the observation point r can be modeled as Es(r) = E_s,theta*theta_hat(ks_hat) + E_s,phi*phi_hat(ks_hat)', with complex components carrying phases e^{j*chi1}, e^{j*chi2}. The SECOND half is correct: there is no coherent surface (PO/Kirchhoff) integral - 'physical optics' and 'Kirchhoff' occur zero times in the report; the diffuse model is a per-patch phenomenological scattering-coefficient / scattering-pattern model (Lambertian / directive / backscattering) with random phases.

wrong_items.claim: Subtitle: 'Even where rays hit, Sionna gives only a path gain, never a scattering integral — so no RCS, at any distance'
wrong_items.why: Same defect as idx 140: 'gives only a path gain' is contradicted by Sionna RT's complex scattered-field model (Eq. 168). The 'never a scattering integral -> no RCS, at any distance' part stands.

wrong_items.claim: Table row: CISSIR (NVIDIA) — sensed = 'no target'; 'No target RCS at all'; family = 'None'
wrong_items.why: FALSIFIED on all three cells, plus a wrong attribution. (a) CISSIR DOES have a target: Table I.D lists 'Target azimuth -39 deg', 'Target distance 40 m', 'Target radar cross section 1 m2', 'Target RX power -81.0 dBm'; Sec. V: 'we simulate a backscatter channel H(t) = S(t) + Hr(t) in a single-target scenario'. (b) It therefore HAS a target RCS - an injected constant 1 m2. (c) Its family is 'Injected' (point target), not 'None'; ray tracing is used for the self-interference channel, not for the target. (d) '(NVIDIA)' is a wrong attribution: the authors are Hernangomez, Fink, Cavalcante and Stanczak (Fraunhofer HHI / TU Berlin lineage); the paper's only NVIDIA mention is 'Sionna(TM), a Python library by Nvidia'.

claims.paper_referred: Sionna / Sionna RT (NVIDIA ray-tracing simulator)
claims.claim_text: 'Sionna returns only a path gain for the drone — it never integrates the scattering over the target surface'
claims.evidence: HALF FALSIFIED. Sionna RT does NOT return 'only a path gain': it returns complex field/channel coefficients. Technical Report Eq. (168) gives the diffusely scattered field explicitly - 'the diffusely scattered field Es(r) at the observation point r can be modeled as Es(r) = E_s,theta*theta_hat(ks_hat) + E_s,phi*phi_hat(ks_hat)', with complex components carrying phases e^{j*chi1}, e^{j*chi2}. The SECOND half is correct: there is no coherent surface (PO/Kirchhoff) integral - 'physical optics' and 'Kirchhoff' occur zero times in the report; the diffuse model is a per-patch phenomenological scattering-coefficient / scattering-pattern model (Lambertian / directive / backscattering) with random phases.

claims.evidence: Content is right for Rel-15 (FR1 SCS 15/30/60 kHz, FR2 SCS 60/120 kHz for data). Two wording defects: 'mu = 15/30/60 kHz' conflates the numerology index mu (0/1/2) with the subcarrier spacing; and FR2 also uses 240 kHz for SSB in Rel-15 and 480/960 kHz in FR2-2.

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: 'Radio frame = 10 ms, containing ten 1 ms subframes'; 'Slots per subframe = 2^μ, giving 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 for μ = 0 to 4'
claims.evidence: 38.211 Sec. 4.3.1 (10 ms frame, ten 1 ms subframes) and Table 4.3.2-1 (slots per frame 10/20/40/80/160 -> slots per subframe 1/2/4/8/16 = 2^mu).

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: 'A slot is the conventional scheduling unit'; '5G also supports shorter mini-slot transmissions'
claims.evidence: Slot-based (type A) scheduling is the conventional unit; 38.214 also defines non-slot-based / mini-slot (type B) PDSCH mapping.

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: 'RE (Resource Element) = one subcarrier × one OFDM symbol'; 'RB (Resource Block) = 12 consecutive subcarriers in frequency'
claims.evidence: 38.211 Sec. 4.4.4: a resource element is one subcarrier in one OFDM symbol; a resource block is 12 consecutive subcarriers in the frequency domain.

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: Resource hierarchy: 'Carrier -> BWP -> RB -> RE'; 'A BWP defines the frequency range where a UE operates inside the wider 5G carrier'
claims.evidence: 38.211 Sec. 4.4.5 (bandwidth part) - a BWP is a contiguous set of PRBs inside a carrier, and the UE operates inside its active BWP.

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: Downlink physical channels: PDSCH carries user data and is dynamically scheduled; PDCCH carries DCI in a CORESET; PBCH carries the MIB and repeats periodically inside the SSB with PBCH DM-RS as its reference symbols
claims.evidence: 38.211 Sec. 7.3: PDSCH (Sec. 7.3.1), PDCCH in a CORESET (Sec. 7.3.2.2 'Control-resource set (CORESET)'), PBCH (Sec. 7.3.3) carrying the MIB inside the SS/PBCH block with PBCH DM-RS.

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: Reference signals: DM-RS for demodulation (tied to PDSCH/PDCCH/PBCH); PT-RS tracks common phase error and matters at high carrier frequency; CSI-RS for channel/beam measurement, configurable periodic / semi-persistent / aperiodic
claims.evidence: 38.211 Sec. 7.4.1 defines DM-RS, PT-RS and CSI-RS; 38.331 configures CSI-RS resources as periodic / semi-persistent / aperiodic.

claims.paper_referred: 3GPP 5G NR standard (Release 15+)
claims.claim_text: 'SSB (Synchronization Signal Block) = PSS + SSS + PBCH + PBCH DM-RS, one composite block'
claims.evidence: VERBATIM: 38.211 Sec. 7.4.3.1 - 'In the time domain, an SS/PBCH block consists of 4 OFDM symbols ... where PSS, SSS, and PBCH with associated DM-RS are mapped to symbols as given by Table 7.4.3.1-1.'
